plain: An HTTP request header that carries an MPP credential when the challenge asked for it, so the Authorization header can keep a bearer token.
ste: A header that holds the payment credential. The server asks for it when Authorization holds a different token.

plain: A request header in which an MPP client lists the method and intent pairs it supports, with optional q weights. The server's challenge stays authoritative.
ste: A header that lists the payment methods and intents that the client can use.

plain: Tying an MPP challenge id to all its parameters, usually with an HMAC-SHA256 over them, so a client cannot change what it pays for and a server can verify statelessly.
ste: The server makes the challenge identifier from the challenge values with a secret key. Thus, nobody can change the values.

plain: A rule set (RFC 8785) that serializes JSON the same way everywhere. MPP encodes the request parameter with it so binding inputs match across implementations.
ste: A standard that writes JSON data in one fixed form.

plain: A rail-specific MPP specification, named by a lowercase id such as tempo, stripe or card, that defines the request and payload fields and how to verify and settle.
ste: A specification for one payment rail. It tells the client how to pay and the server how to verify.

plain: In the Visa-authored MPP card method, the party that provisions a network token and cryptogram for the client and encrypts them for the server.
ste: The party that gets a card token for the client and encrypts it for the server.

plain: In the MPP card method, the PSP or acquirer that decrypts the token for the merchant server and requests authorization from the card network.
ste: The payment provider that decrypts the card token and asks the card network for approval.

plain: The party that pays network fees for a transaction. In MPP Tempo methods the server can co-sign as fee payer; Stripe's hostedFeePayer makes Stripe pay.
ste: The party that pays the network fee for a transaction.

plain: Ending an MPP session channel by agreement: the client sends a final voucher and the server closes on chain, capturing only what was spent and refunding the rest.
ste: The server closes the channel with the last voucher. The server keeps the used amount and returns the remainder.

plain: Ending an MPP session channel without the server: the client calls requestClose, waits a grace period of at least 15 minutes, then withdraws what is left.
ste: The client closes the channel without the server. The client waits 15 minutes or more, then takes back the money.

plain: The Stripe merchant identity that the stripe MPP method puts in methodDetails.networkId so an SPT can be scoped to that seller.
ste: The Stripe identifier of the seller. The payment token works only for this seller.

plain: A public explorer by Merit Systems that indexes MPP servers, agents, transactions and volume, mostly on Tempo.
ste: A public web site that shows MPP payments and servers.

plain: A Tempo key authorization with limits that the payer signs once so a server can collect recurring MPP subscription charges.
ste: A key with limits that the payer approves. The server uses it to collect each subscription payment.

plain: The Tempo precompile that holds session deposits in MPP session protocol v2, replacing the v1 escrow contract.
ste: The built-in Tempo function that holds the deposit for a session, version 2.
